assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling turned aryl amine formation from a harsh, narrow-scope problem into a routine, general bond construction. It is among the most heavily used reactions in pharmaceutical and agrochemical process chemistry and in materials work, and the ligand-design logic (bulky electron-rich phosphines) transferred to many other couplings. This is exactly the kind of method that changed how chemists everywhere build bonds, and it extends the 2010 cross-coupling prize into C-heteroatom bonds.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general catalytic amination independently and in parallel in the mid-1990s and then led the ligand and mechanistic development. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work was a precursor but not the general catalytic method; I regard the two-person configuration as the fairest, though priority arguments around Migita/Kosugi could be raised.
assessment.maturity: Mature: three decades of independent confirmation, industrial scale use, and a stable mechanistic picture. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as too close to the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Weight of the Kosugi/Migita precedent for priority; I am relying on memory rather than verified literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened a general way to generate radicals and radical ions under mild conditions with simple light sources, and enabled new disconnections, late-stage functionalisation and dual-catalytic strategies. Adoption in academic and industrial synthesis is very broad, and it is conceptually simple to explain: light plus a catalyst replaces stoichiometric reagents.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread over many groups. Yoon, Stephenson and Nicewicz independently introduced key synthetic applications of Ru/Ir and organic photocatalysts around 2008-2012, while MacMillan (already a 2021 laureate) and others made major contributions, as did Fukuzumi, Konig and Melchiorre in the underlying photochemistry. A three-person prize is plausible but the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature, with over fifteen years of wide use and confirmed mechanisms, though ongoing debate about mechanistic details (chain versus catalytic pathways) in some reactions.
uncertainties: Whether MacMillan's prior prize excludes or complicates his inclusion.
Contested priority among early groups and the photochemistry precedents.
Some claimed photoredox reactions have been questioned on mechanistic grounds.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Selective catalytic C-H functionalisation changes the logic of retrosynthesis by treating ordinary C-H bonds as functional groups. Ligand-accelerated and directing-group-based methods from Yu and Pd(II)/Pd(IV) chemistry from Sanford made site selectivity controllable and the reactions usable in total synthesis and in medicinal chemistry. Strong on both generality and conceptual novelty, though individual methods are still less routine than cross-coupling.
assessment.attribution: Yu (ligand and template control, remote C-H activation) and Sanford (Pd and later other metal catalysis with oxidants, mechanistic work) are the clearest leaders. Hartwig (borylation) and Daugulis contributed important parts, and the field's pioneers in stoichiometric C-H activation sit under another candidate, so the line of credit is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature but still developing; industrial adoption is growing and strongest for borylation, less so for directed Pd chemistry. Recognition may be slightly early.
uncertainties: Allocation between directed C-H activation, borylation and earlier organometallic work.
Extent of routine use in industry relative to its academic prominence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs showed that sterically hindered Lewis acid/base combinations can heterolytically split H2 and activate other small molecules without metals, giving metal-free hydrogenation. This is a new chemical concept, clear and teachable, with a body of follow-up work in main-group chemistry and catalysis.
assessment.attribution: Stephan's 2006 metal-free H2 activation and Erker's contributions (including reversible activation and FLP reactivity with olefins and other substrates) form a natural two-person credit. Early work by Piers, Tamm, and others on related systems may be cited but is generally not seen as the central discovery.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature: well confirmed and widely studied, but practical impact in synthesis and industry is more limited than for the top candidates.
uncertainties: Possible claims from related early work on borane/phosphine reactivity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The isolation of stable carbenes (imidazolylidenes and cyclic alkyl amino carbenes) established a new class of stable species and produced N-heterocyclic carbene ligands that are essential in modern metathesis and cross-coupling catalysts, plus organocatalysis. Impact on synthetic practice is large and has been demonstrated across many later reactions.
assessment.attribution: Arduengo's 1991 crystalline carbene is the decisive discovery. Bertrand's earlier stable phosphinocarbene and later CAAC carbenes are major, and Nolan's work established NHCs as ligands. Bode and Rovis contributed on organocatalysis, a different aspect, so the compound nature of the candidate complicates the prize.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of confirmation and wide use. Timing is not premature.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should focus on isolation of the carbene or on its ligand and organocatalyst use.
Priority issues for Bertrand's earlier phosphinocarbene.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phosphoramidite chemistry made reliable, automated solid-phase DNA synthesis possible, underpinning PCR primers, sequencing, gene synthesis and oligonucleotide therapeutics. It is a clear case of a chemical method that enabled an entire field and remains in use essentially unchanged after four decades.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers developed the phosphoramidite method in the early 1980s and is the clear primary contributor. Hood's role was in automation of the synthesizer, which is more instrument engineering than chemistry, so I would not credit him in the proposed configuration.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and overdue by timing; the chemistry is universally used.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants to include the instrument developers.
Possible interplay with other nucleic-acid chemistry candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom transfer radical polymerization provides controlled radical polymerization of many monomers with defined molecular weights, architectures and end groups, and it is used for functional materials and polymer design. It is a general and conceptually simple method that made well-defined polymers accessible with a standard radical chemistry setup.
assessment.attribution: Sawamoto (Ru-catalysed living radical polymerization) and Matyjaszewski (Cu-catalysed ATRP) published in 1995; Matyjaszewski is the main developer, with Sawamoto and Kamigaito as co-discoverers. Wang is a co-author on the first Matyjaszewski paper, but I treat the three-person configuration as clearer. RAFT is a parallel competing method that complicates the allocation of the field.
assessment.maturity: Mature with widespread use; industrial impact is real but less dominant than the synthetic organic methods ranked above.
uncertainties: Competition with RAFT and the question of whether both should be recognised.
Importance relative to organic synthetic methods.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors use engineered deaminases fused to a Cas9 nickase to convert one base into another without double-strand breaks, a protein-engineering and nucleic-acid chemistry advance with fast therapeutic uptake and clinical trials. Clearly high impact, but I ask what is new chemically; much of the novelty lies in biochemical engineering of an existing CRISPR system.
assessment.attribution: Liu's lab developed cytosine and adenine base editors, with Komor and Gaudelli as lead authors of the key papers. Nishida and Kondo reported a deaminase-Cas fusion in parallel, creating a modest priority question.
assessment.maturity: Relatively recent (2016-2017) but quickly confirmed in many labs, with early clinical results. Recognition might be premature compared with the more established methods, and CRISPR itself has already been recognised.
uncertainties: Whether the chemistry content is sufficient, given the 2020 CRISPR prize.
Long-term clinical validation is still emerging.
Priority issue with the Nishida and Kondo work.
